oneLiner: The only proven non-NVIDIA inference architecture at scale, valued at ~55-60x current-year sales on the strength of a $10B OpenAI deal, an AWS beachhead, and extreme UAE customer concentration.
thesis: Genuine architectural differentiation: wafer-scale SRAM (WSE-3: ~900K cores, 44GB on-chip, ~21PB/s) keeps weights on-die; independent tests show 3-6x Groq's tokens/sec on identical open models.
Inference is becoming the dominant AI workload and speed/latency (agentic chains, reasoning models) is exactly where wafer-scale differentiates.

Anchor validation: $10B multi-year OpenAI compute deal (750MW) signed pre-IPO; AWS is the first hyperscaler to deploy Cerebras in its own data centers (Bedrock pairs Trainium prefill with CS-3 decode); AMD partnership (Jul 2026) fuses Instinct/Helios with wafer-scale.
The bet is execution: FY2026 guide (~$860M) is capacity-constrained; ramping toward OpenAI delivery requires flawless manufacturing and data-center scaling on a TSMC process it does not control.

latestQuarter.label: Q1 FY2026 (ended Mar 31, 2026; reported Jun 23, 2026) - Q2 due Aug 12, 2026
points: Core non-GAAP operating loss -$3.5M (-2% margin); GAAP net loss $14.0M.
Guide: Q2 core revenue ~$194M (+88% YoY); FY2026 revenue $855-865M, capacity-constrained.
Stock fell ~47% from post-IPO highs at one point on margin-guidance confusion; CEO called it misunderstood.

segments: Hardware (CS-3 systems) plus fast-growing cloud/inference services; positioning has shifted decisively to inference.
Customer concentration extreme: FY2025 was 62% MBZUAI + 24% G42 = 86% UAE entities; post-Q1 expanded G42 and AWS arrangements.
competitive: NVIDIA is the default and acquired Groq for $20B in Dec 2025 - a direct fast-inference response.
AMD went the other way: July 2026 partnership integrating wafer-scale with Helios (claimed 5x tokens/sec/watt - vendor figure).
Risk: commodity GPU token prices falling faster than the speed premium holds.
moat: Wafer-scale SRAM is hard to replicate and demonstrably fastest at inference today, but the moat is narrow: it depends on one TSMC process with no long-term supply agreement and no second source, and NVIDIA can buy or build fast-inference capability while bundling an unmatched software ecosystem.
risks: Customer concentration: 86% of FY2025 revenue from UAE entities; the OpenAI deal deepens single-counterparty exposure.
Scale-up execution: capacity-constrained guide; $10B OpenAI delivery requires flawless ramping.
NVIDIA-Groq squeeze on both demand and TSMC supply priority.
TSMC single-source dependency; process not portable.
Margin opacity: UAE deal structures (warrants, leases) cloud unit economics; the post-Q1 selloff was a margin scare.
Lockup: ~28M Class A shares tradeable two days after the Q2 report (mid-Aug 2026).
catalysts: Q2 FY2026 earnings Aug 12, 2026 (tomorrow); lockup release ~Aug 14.
pricedIn: ~$48-51B market cap vs $855-865M FY2026 guided revenue = ~55-60x current-year sales. IPO'd May 14, 2026 at $185 ($5.55B raised, largest US tech IPO since Uber), opened at $385. Debate: does OpenAI plus AWS distribution justify pricing it as the next NVIDIA, or is a capacity-constrained, UAE-concentrated, sub-$1B-revenue company priced for a flawless multi-year ramp that TSMC allocation and NVIDIA-Groq could derail?

scenarios.bear: Q2 shows flat sequential revenue, margin questions resurface, the lockup dumps ~28M shares into a nervous tape; OpenAI consolidates onto NVIDIA/Groq and internal silicon; TSMC allocation caps growth; multiple compresses toward 15-20x sales (below $100).
scenarios.base: FY2026 lands ~$860M; OpenAI revenue ramps in 2027 toward a multi-billion run-rate; AWS Bedrock broadens the base beyond the UAE; losses stay near breakeven; stock digests the lockup and holds a 40-60x sales band (~$200-290).
scenarios.bull: Q2 beats with a raise; OpenAI's 750MW deploys ahead of plan; AMD partnership wins agentic-inference share as reasoning workloads explode; 2027 revenue runs well past $2B and scarcity value drives the stock toward its $385 opening print.

valPresets.note: Pre-scale company with two public quarters; TTM revenue uses Yahoo's trailing figure. Values the terminal business off a revenue path, horizon FCF margin, and exit multiple.
